core.title: Make each tracking-plan item's identity mirror its path
core.given: Telemetry is adopted, and a tracking-plan item file exists under the telemetry root. The root's default location and its configured override come from the profile; a configured root replaces the default. The file may be new, changed or unchanged.
core.when: You plan, author, rename or review a tracking-plan item at <telemetry root>/<theme>/<artifact>/{event|trace|metric|log}.<plane>[.<measure>]
core.then: Make the item's declared identity mirror its path: id = telemetry:{kind}:{plane}:{theme}:{artifact}[:{measure}], logical_artifact = telemetry:{theme}:{artifact}, and the file name's kind, plane and measure equal the declared fields.
prefer: Name the file for what it is, then derive id and logical_artifact from the path.

Keep the item valid against the stack's tracking-plan schema. Declare id, a SemVer version, logical_artifact, kind, plane, owner, purpose, acceptances, properties and required. Optionally add forbidden_properties. Give each property a type, classification and cardinality. Every `required` name must be declared in `properties`. Metric dimensions are optional, but each one present must declare cardinality.
Give every metric item a measure segment (metric.<plane>.<measure> in the file name, id ending :{measure}). Never give an event, trace or log item a measure segment.
avoid: Renaming a file or hand-editing an id so that the path and the identity drift apart
Declaring the same concrete id in two files
Putting notes, indexes or generated bundles under the telemetry root
Treating a logical artifact as an exporter event
unless: Telemetry is not adopted: there is no telemetry root and no acceptance telemetry declaration. Adoption means creating the tree or making the first acceptance decision.
core.why: The telemetry tree is a registry, not a suggestion. The path is the authority for identity, so a renamed file or a hand-edited id cannot drift apart silently.
evidence: Every tracking-plan item file under the resolved telemetry root validates against the tracking-plan schema.

For each file, the kind, plane and measure parsed from the file name match the declared fields. The id equals telemetry:{kind}:{plane}:{theme}:{artifact}[:{measure}] and the logical_artifact equals telemetry:{theme}:{artifact}, both derived from the path.
No concrete id is declared by more than one file.
With no telemetry root and no acceptance telemetry declaration, the check emits no findings.
In an adopted repository, an unchanged item that is invalid is still reported. Checks cover all items, not only changed ones.
Every metric item has a measure segment in its file name and id. No event, trace or log item has one.
verification: Severity 2, strict disposition: the check fails on every finding; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.
Scope: the telemetry root, the versioned tracking-plan source of truth, resolved through the profile. A configured root replaces the default and does not add to it; only the resolved root is scanned.

Item path grammar: <telemetry root>/<theme>/<artifact>/{event|trace|metric|log}.<plane>[.<measure>] with the item file suffix taken from the profile's item pattern. Metric items carry a measure segment; event, trace and log items never do.

Division of labor: local shape is the tracking-plan schema's job — required identity fields, URN grammar, SemVer core version, property declarations with classification and cardinality, and metric dimensions that declare cardinality. This rule covers the cross-artifact checks the schema cannot see: (1) the file name's kind, plane and measure match the declared fields; (2) the id equals telemetry:{kind}:{plane}:{theme}:{artifact}[:{measure}] derived from the path; (3) the logical_artifact equals telemetry:{theme}:{artifact} from the path; (4) the names in `required` are a subset of the `properties` keys; (5) no two files declare the same concrete id.
Item fields: id, version, logical_artifact, kind, plane, owner, purpose, acceptances, properties, required. Optional: forbidden_properties and, for metrics only, dimensions.

Identity model: a concrete item is a telemetry URN with kind and plane, telemetry:{kind}:{plane}:{theme}:{artifact}[:{measure}]. A logical artifact, telemetry:{theme}:{artifact}, is the stable architectural identity of an observable outcome; it is not an exporter event — the concrete items under it are.
Every file of the tracking-plan item format under the root is judged as an item. There is no allow-list for non-item files of that format.
Adoption gate: with no telemetry root and no acceptance telemetry declaration anywhere, emit nothing. Installing or upgrading the convention tooling must not fail a repository that has not opted in.
After adoption, the check covers all items under the resolved root regardless of diff status; an unchanged item that is invalid is still reported.

values: telemetry adopted: a telemetry root exists, or an acceptance declares telemetry

fires: A planner adds a new tracking-plan item file under the telemetry root for a new observable outcome
A tracking-plan item file is renamed or moved, and its id or logical_artifact no longer matches its new path
An existing, unchanged tracking-plan item in an adopted repository has an id that does not match its path
A metric item has no measure segment, or an event, trace or log item has one
The repository configures a non-default telemetry root, and an item under that configured root is checked
doesNotFire: The repository has no telemetry root and no acceptance declares telemetry (it has not opted in)
Item files outside the resolved telemetry root, including files under the default root when a different root is configured
Files under the telemetry root that are not of the tracking-plan item format

profileRequirements.meaning: Where the telemetry (tracking-plan) registry lives: the default root, the config knob that overrides it, and that the override replaces the default rather than adding to it. This is a second, simultaneous plan registry alongside the one carried by roots.plan, which in this stack is bound to the source plan root.
profileRequirements.bunValue: `telemetry/` by default, configurable as topology.telemetry_root in atdd-bun.yaml; the configured root replaces the default and does not add to it

profileRequirements.meaning: The repository file in which the telemetry root override is declared.

Path pattern of one tracking-plan item under the telemetry root, including the theme/artifact segments, the kind.plane[.measure] file-name grammar and the item file suffix. A second, simultaneous plan-item grammar alongside the one carried by layout.plan_item.

proposedKeys.meaning: Root of the telemetry tracking-plan registry: the versioned source of truth for planned observations; a configured root replaces the default and does not add to it.
proposedKeys.bunValue: `telemetry/` by default, configurable as topology.telemetry_root in atdd-bun.yaml
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: roots.plan is the general plan-artifact root key and is not restricted to any one artifact kind. The need is cardinality, not restriction: a profile holds ONE value per key, and this stack runs two distinct plan registries at the same time — roots.plan is bound in this stack to topology.plan_root (default plan, the vocabulary's own Bun example) for the source plan tree, while the telemetry tracking plan is a separate, simultaneous registry with its own default (telemetry/) and its own override knob (topology.telemetry_root). Binding the telemetry root to roots.plan would collide with that already-bound plan_root value and point the check at the wrong tree, so the second registry needs a second root key.

proposedKeys.meaning: Path pattern of one tracking-plan item under the telemetry registry root, carrying the theme/artifact segments, the kind.plane[.measure] file-name grammar and the item file suffix.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: layout.plan_item is the general per-stack pattern for one plan artifact and is not restricted to WMBTs. Again the need is cardinality: it is a single slot per stack, bound in this stack to the plan-root registry's pattern (<plan_root>/<wagon_dir>/<wmbt_id>.yaml, the vocabulary's example), while the telemetry registry's items follow a different, simultaneous grammar under a different root (<telemetry_root>/<theme>/<artifact>/{event|trace|metric|log}.<plane>[.<measure>].json). One pattern slot cannot carry both grammars, so the second registry needs a second item-pattern key.

neutralityNotes: The telemetry data model — kinds (event/trace/metric/log), planes, measures, the item field list and the telemetry:{...} URN grammar — is treated as stack-neutral convention content, because the tracking plan is an ATDD artifact whose shape does not depend on the runtime; only its serialization suffix is profile data. Profile keys roots.telemetry and layout.telemetry_item are proposed rather than reusing roots.plan and layout.plan_item: those existing keys are general plan-artifact keys (not WMBT-only), but a profile holds one value per key and this stack runs two simultaneous plan registries — the plan-root registry already occupies both slots (the vocabulary's Bun examples bind them to topology.plan_root and <plan_root>/<wagon_dir>/<wmbt_id>.yaml), so the telemetry registry needs its own slots. If the owner instead prefers to extend the vocabulary with a parametric plan-registry form (e.g. roots.plan.<registry>), the two proposals should fold into it. What could not be made neutral: the default root path and its config knob (profile: roots.telemetry, declared in roots.config), the concrete item path pattern including the .json suffix (profile: layout.telemetry_item), the schema document name telemetry-plan.schema.json (bunOnly: prefer[1], evidence[0], verifier_detail[2]), the adoption finding id telemetry_adopted (bunOnly), and the worked fix example (bunOnly: verifier_detail[8]). Severity 2 and the strict disposition are kept in core verification, not the profile, per the not-profile-keys rule; the validator ref planner_telemetry_plan stays with the realization.
